explain: The frame every web page starts with. head holds information, body holds what you see.
example: The first thing you type in every new .html file.

explain: Tags that name the parts of a page. They work like div, but say what each part is for.
example: A blog: header with the logo, main with the posts, footer with the copyright.

explain: div is a plain box for grouping things, usually so CSS can style the group.
example: Wrapping each product on a shop page in a card.

explain: Headings go from h1 (biggest) to h6 (smallest). p is a paragraph.
example: An article title, section titles, and the body text.

explain: A link. href is where it goes.
example: A menu that links to your other pages.

explain: Shows an image. alt describes it for screen readers, and shows if the image fails to load.
A form: a label, a box to type in, and a button.
id names one unique element. class groups many. CSS and JavaScript use both to find elements.
example: Styling every .lead paragraph, and finding #intro from JavaScript.

explain: A bulleted list. Use ol instead of ul for a numbered list.
